en/dialogue/07/078ca0b0492e1d73.mp3.text:
f:Hello. Can I help you?
m:Hi. A library card, please.
f:Sure. What's your name?
m:Ravi Sharma.
f:How do you spell your last name?
m:S-H-A-R-M-A.
f:Thanks. And how old are you, Ravi?
m:I'm nineteen.
f:What's your phone number?
m:It's five five five, oh one seven two.
f:Great. Here's your card. Have a nice day!

en/dialogue/0d/0d57cb734b3cbbd4.mp3.text:
f:So, show me your new apartment!
m:OK! This is the living room.
f:Nice! Is that a new sofa?
m:Yes, it is. It's next to the window.
f:And where's the TV?
m:It's on the wall, opposite the sofa.
f:Where's the kitchen?
m:It's behind the living room. It's very small.
f:Have you got two bedrooms?
m:Yes. My bedroom is next to the bathroom.
f:And where's your cat?
m:Ha! She's under the bed, as usual.

en/dialogue/0d/0dba32ae4c1b5534.mp3.text:
m:Hi! What would you like?
f:Hi. Can I have a large coffee, please?
m:Sure. With milk?
f:Yes, please. But no sugar.
m:Would you like anything to eat?
f:Yes. A blueberry muffin, please.
m:And I'd like a hot chocolate.
m:Small, medium or large?
m:Small, please.
m:For here or to go?
f:For here, thanks.
m:OK. That's twelve dollars, please.

en/dialogue/1d/1ddede4722dd772c.mp3.text:
f:Excuse me. Is the art museum near here?
m:Yes, it's about ten minutes on foot.
f:Great! How do I get there?
m:Go straight for two blocks.
f:Two blocks. OK.
m:Then turn left at the traffic lights.
f:Left at the traffic lights…
m:Cross the square. The museum is opposite the park.
f:Opposite the park. Thank you so much!
m:You're welcome. Oh, and don't take Bridge Street!
f:Why not?
m:It's closed today. Enjoy the museum!

en/dialogue/1e/1e2645bcae3f3fe2.mp3.text:
f:Kofi, hurry! What time is it?
m:It's twenty to seven.
f:And the movie starts at seven?
m:No, at quarter past seven.
f:Oh, good. We aren't late, then.
m:Is it a long movie?
f:Yes, two hours. It ends at quarter past nine.
m:And the last bus home?
f:It's at half past nine.
m:Perfect. Popcorn time!

en/dialogue/3a/3af690bbe5ddabbb.mp3.text:
f:Nico, look at this jacket!
m:The green one? Hmm, it's OK.
f:No, not that one. This blue jacket.
m:Oh, I like that. It's nice.
f:And these jeans? What do you think?
m:They're great. Are they black?
f:No, they're dark blue.
m:Look at those shoes over there!
f:The white shoes? They're cool.
m:I need some shoes for work.
f:Let's ask the salesperson.
m:Good idea!

en/dialogue/40/406aa0f784da3ba0.mp3.text:
m:Good morning. Can I buy two tickets to Ocean City here?
f:Yes, you can. One-way or round-trip?
m:Round-trip, please. We're going to come back tonight.
f:OK. The next train leaves at nine forty.
m:Nine forty? And how long is the trip?
f:About two hours. It arrives at eleven forty.
m:Great. How much are the tickets?
f:They're twenty-eight dollars each, so fifty-six dollars.
m:Can I pay by card?
f:Yes, of course.
m:Which platform is it?
f:Platform six. It's on the left, next to the café.
m:And what time is the last train back?
f:It's at eight fifteen this evening.
m:Thank you very much!
f:You're welcome. Have a nice day at the beach!

en/dialogue/42/427f00bd5ad2913f.mp3.text:
f:Hi! Can I help you?
m:Yes, please. I'm looking for a sweater.
f:What size are you?
m:Medium, I think.
f:We've got this one in blue and gray.
m:The gray one is nice. Can I try it on?
f:Sure. The fitting room is over there.
m:Hmm, it's too big. Have you got a small?
f:Yes, here you are.
m:Perfect, it fits! How much is it?
f:Forty-nine dollars. Or two for seventy!
m:Just one, thanks. Can I pay by card?

en/dialogue/49/492781c2784f3889.mp3.text:
f:Hi there! Are you ready to order?
m:Yes, please. What soups have you got today?
f:We've got tomato soup and chicken soup.
m:I'd like the tomato soup, please.
f:Would you like some bread with it?
m:Yes, please.
f:And can I have a cheese sandwich?
f:Sorry, we haven't got any cheese today.
f:Oh no! Have you got any salads?
f:Yes, a green salad and a chicken salad.
f:The green salad, please. And an orange juice.
f:Anything to drink for you, sir?
m:Just water, thanks.
f:OK. One soup with bread, one green salad, an orange juice and a water.
f:How much is that?
f:That's nineteen dollars, please.

en/dialogue/5a/5a1e6a9a88216c00.mp3.text:
f:Pedro, are you free on Tuesday?
m:No, sorry. I always work on Tuesdays.
f:What about Wednesday evening?
m:I usually go to the gym on Wednesday.
f:How often do you go to the gym?
m:Three times a week. And you?
f:Never! I don't like the gym.
m:Ha! Do you work on Thursday?
f:No, I don't. I'm free on Thursday.
m:Great! Thursday at six, at the library?
f:OK. See you on Thursday!

en/dialogue/5d/5d9010bbeb6f47e8.mp3.text:
f:Good morning, Mr. Davis!
m:Good morning, Ana. How are you?
f:I'm very well, thank you. And you?
m:I'm fine, thanks.
m:Hi, Ana! How's it going?
f:Hi, Ben! Good, thanks. And you?
m:Not bad, but I'm tired today.
f:Oh no! Coffee time, then!
m:Goodbye, Ana. Have a nice evening!
f:Thank you, you too. See you tomorrow!

en/dialogue/64/641c4c6175dd655f.mp3.text:
m:Good evening. A table for two?
f:Yes, please.
m:Here's the menu. Are you ready to order?
f:Yes. Have you got any vegetarian dishes?
m:Yes, we've got a vegetable curry. It's spicy.
f:Perfect. And some rice, please.
m:I'd like the chicken soup and the fish.
m:Sorry, we haven't got any fish tonight.
m:Oh. The chicken salad, then.
m:Would you like some water?
f:Yes, please. A bottle of water.
m:Mmm, this is delicious! Can we have the check, please?

en/dialogue/6e/6e1465d67241a723.mp3.text:
f:Good morning! What would you like?
m:Hi! I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, please.
f:Sure. Anything else?
m:Yes, some onions and some potatoes.
f:Here you are. The apples are very fresh today.
m:OK, six apples, please. And some bananas.
f:Would you like some cheese too?
m:Yes, please. A small piece.
f:And bread? It's from this morning.
m:No, thanks. I've got some bread at home.
f:OK. That's fifteen dollars.
m:Here you are. Thank you!

en/dialogue/7c/7ca9fc6e037fd6ac.mp3.text:
m:Hi, Sienna! What are you doing?
f:I'm sitting at home. It's snowing in Toronto!
m:Snowing? Here in Sydney it's summer.
f:Lucky you! What's the weather like?
m:It's sunny and very hot.
f:And what are you doing now?
m:I'm walking on the beach!
f:Oh no! I'm wearing two sweaters.
m:Ha! Is it very cold?
f:Yes, it's minus ten degrees.
m:Brr! I love summer in January!
f:And I love hot chocolate in January!

en/dialogue/8c/8c05e974d1407310.mp3.text:
f:Hi! Can I help you?
m:Yes, please. I'm looking for some running shoes.
f:OK. What size are you?
m:Ten, I think.
f:How about these blue shoes? They're very popular.
m:Hmm. Have you got them in black?
f:Yes, we have. Here you are. Size ten.
m:Thanks. Can I try them on?
f:Of course. Sit here.
m:Oh, they're too small. Have you got an eleven?
f:Let me look… Yes! Here's an eleven.
m:Perfect. These fit. How much are they?
f:They're on sale. Only sixty-five dollars.
m:Great! Can I pay by card?
f:Sure.

en/dialogue/8d/8d2e9943ab9991cd.mp3.text:
f:Hi! I'm Daniela. I'm new here.
m:Hi, Daniela. I'm Joon. Welcome to the neighborhood!
f:Thanks! Is there a supermarket near here?
m:Yes, there is. It's on Oak Street.
f:Great. And are there any good cafés?
m:Yes, there are two cafés in the square.
f:Is there a gym?
m:No, there isn't. But there's a nice park.
f:Perfect. I love parks!
m:And there's a bus stop next to the bank.
f:Thank you, Joon. That's very helpful!

en/dialogue/8d/8de14d63f825b612.mp3.text:
f:Hamid, what do you do in your free time?
m:I love cooking. Indian food, Italian food…
f:Really? I hate cooking!
m:So what do you like doing?
f:I like dancing and listening to music.
m:What's your favorite music?
f:Salsa! I go dancing every Friday.
m:Cool! I don't like dancing very much.
f:Do you like sports?
m:Yes, I play soccer on Sundays.
f:I like watching soccer — on TV!
m:Ha! That's a hobby too!

en/dialogue/8e/8e631c407bd7d143.mp3.text:
f:Excuse me. How can I get downtown?
m:You can take the train or a taxi.
f:Is the train expensive?
m:No, it's cheap. It's five dollars.
f:Can I buy a ticket here?
m:Yes, you can. Use this machine.
f:Can I pay by card?
m:Yes. A one-way or a round-trip ticket?
f:One-way, please. Which platform?
m:Platform two. The next train is at ten fifteen.
f:And where do I get off?
m:Get off at Clark Street. That's downtown.

en/dialogue/9e/9ecfbd0c07360c5a.mp3.text:
m:Lin, you get up very early!
f:Yes, at half past five.
m:Half past five? Why?
f:I'm a baker. I start work at seven.
m:Wow. I get up at nine!
f:Lucky you! And your class?
m:It starts at ten. I have breakfast at a café.
f:I have breakfast at the bakery.
m:And you finish work at three?
f:Yes. Then I go to the gym.
m:I go to bed at one in the morning!
f:Ha! I go to bed at nine.

en/dialogue/c8/c8ff664978c0a357.mp3.text:
f:So, Omar, what do you do?
m:I'm a nurse. I work at City Hospital.
f:Really? My brother's a nurse too!
m:And you? What's your job?
f:I'm an engineer. I work in a big office.
m:Are your colleagues nice?
f:Yes, they are. They're very friendly.
m:Are your parents engineers too?
f:No! My mom's a teacher and my dad's retired.
m:My parents are cooks. They've got a small restaurant.
f:A restaurant? Great! What's the name?

en/dialogue/cf/cfecc8d43095ce8f.mp3.text:
f:Good afternoon, Bay View Hotel. How can I help you?
m:Hello. I'd like to book a room, please.
f:Of course. When are you going to arrive?
m:On Friday. For two nights.
f:A single or a double room?
m:A double, please. How much is it?
f:It's ninety-five dollars a night.
m:Is breakfast included?
f:Yes, it is. Breakfast is from seven to ten.
m:Great. Can I check in early?
f:Yes, after twelve. What's your name, please?
m:Karim Haddad. H-A-double D-A-D.

en/dialogue/d0/d0d53e79e1e4e1bf.mp3.text:
f:Hello, everyone. I'm Grace, your teacher.
f:Hi, Grace! My name's Lucía.
m:And I'm Kenji. Nice to meet you.
f:Nice to meet you too. Are you Chinese?
m:No, I'm not. I'm Japanese. And you?
f:I'm Spanish. I'm from Valencia.
f:And where do you live now, Lucía?
f:I live here in Toronto.
m:Me too! But my English isn't very good.
f:That's OK. We're here to learn!

en/dialogue/db/db041615184a36de.mp3.text:
f:Excuse me, how much is this bag?
m:It's thirty-five pounds.
f:Thirty-five? That's expensive!
m:But it's a very good bag.
f:And how much are these sunglasses?
m:They're on sale. Only fifteen pounds.
f:Fifteen or fifty?
m:Fifteen. One, five.
f:Great. I'd like the sunglasses, please.
m:Cash or card?
f:Card, please. Here you are.
m:Thanks! Enjoy your sunglasses!

en/dialogue/e5/e562712d716c5a28.mp3.text:
f:Is this your family, Jamal?
m:Yes. This is my mom, and that's my dad.
f:And who's the little girl?
m:That's my sister's daughter, Zara.
f:Oh, she's cute! How old is she?
m:She's four. Her brother is seven.
f:Are your grandparents in the photo?
m:Yes, my grandma's here, on the left.
f:Is your family big?
m:Yes! I've got three sisters and ten cousins.
f:Wow! My family's very small.

en/dialogue/ea/ea228f90f0efd1da.mp3.text:
f:So, what does your cousin look like?
m:Well, he's tall and very young.
f:Has he got short hair?
m:No, he's got long curly hair.
f:Is he the man with the glasses?
m:No, Dev hasn't got glasses.
f:What about the man with the beard?
m:Yes, that's Dev! He's got a beard now!
f:He looks friendly.
m:He is. And he's very funny.
m:Tom! Hi! And you're Priya, right?

en/dialogue/ee/ee18f9299be3dfdb.mp3.text:
m:Hi, Ruth! Are you free on Saturday?
f:Not in the morning. I work on Saturdays.
m:How about Saturday afternoon?
f:Yes, I'm free then. What do you want to do?
m:Let's go to the beach!
f:Hmm, I don't really like the beach.
m:OK. How about going to the movies?
f:Maybe. Why don't we have a picnic in the park?
m:Good idea! I love picnics.
f:Let's meet at the park café at two.
m:Perfect. Can I bring my sister, Tess?
f:Of course! See you on Saturday!

en/dialogue/f0/f00ce1a3092ce209.mp3.text:
m:Any plans for the weekend, Asha?
f:Yes! I'm going to go camping.
m:Camping? Where?
f:In the mountains, with my brother and his kids.
m:Great! Is it going to be cold?
f:Maybe, but we've got warm sweaters. And you?
m:Nothing special. I'm going to sleep late.
f:Are you going to see your friends?
m:Yes, we're going to have a barbecue on Sunday.
f:Sounds fun! Have a great weekend!
m:You too! Take a lot of photos!

en/dialogue/f3/f33084f2fee4ab5d.mp3.text:
f:Hi, Bruno! What are you doing?
m:Hi, Lucy. I'm watching a movie at home.
f:It's raining here. Is it raining there?
m:Yes, it's raining and it's very windy.
f:Are you free on Saturday?
m:Yes, I am. Why?
f:Let's go to the beach!
m:But the weather is terrible!
f:Not on Saturday. It's going to be sunny and hot.
m:Really? OK, why not?
f:Great. Do you want to take a picnic?
m:Good idea. I love picnics. I can make sandwiches.
f:And I can bring some fruit and drinks.
m:What time?
f:How about ten o'clock at the bus stop?
m:Perfect. See you on Saturday!
